generation_notes: Revised to exactly 14 structurally valid seeds using only documented EtherNet/IP encapsulation commands, 24-byte encapsulation header fields, little-endian field ordering, Common Packet Format item structure, and named CIP common service codes from the supplied sources. Unsupported issue claims were removed. All SendRRData seeds now include the documented command-specific prefix of 4-byte interface handle and 2-byte timeout before CPF data, and all SendUnitData seeds use the documented Connected Address Item plus Connected Data Item combination. Encapsulation length fields were recalculated to match the actual command-specific byte counts and kept even where the serializer notes require even command-specific data length. CIP payloads are conservative Message Router style requests with path-size bytes matching the included path words and optional small service data blocks for mutation-friendly coverage.
coverage_summary: strategies: baseline_valid, field_interaction, function_code_coverage, length_boundary_valid, parser_depth, stateful_valid
target_operations: Get_Attribute_Single, Get_Attributes_All, RegisterSession, SendRRData, SendUnitData, Service Not Supported, Set_Attribute_Single, Set_Attributes_All, Start, Stop, UnregisterSession

sequences.title: Canonical valid RegisterSession
sequences.purpose: Provide a canonical RegisterSession request with a complete encapsulation header and the conservative 4-byte command-specific payload used by the previous strong seed.
sequences.expected_behavior: The target should accept the 24-byte encapsulation header and parse a valid RegisterSession request with a 4-byte command-specific body.
constraints_preserved: Command 0x0065 is encoded little-endian as 6500.
Length field is 0x0004 and matches the 4 bytes after the header.
Session handle is zero for initial registration.
Status is 0x00000000 in the request.
Sender context is present as 8 bytes.
Options are 0x00000000.
Total outer header size is 24 bytes.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: No issue enhancement is used; this is a conservative valid baseline request.

sequences.title: Discovery prelude then RegisterSession
sequences.purpose: Exercise sequential parsing through valid discovery commands before a final RegisterSession request.
sequences.expected_behavior: The implementation should parse two complete zero-length encapsulation commands and then a valid RegisterSession frame without framing errors.
constraints_preserved: Each message has a complete 24-byte encapsulation header.
ListServices uses command 0x0004 with zero payload length.
ListIdentity uses command 0x0063 with zero payload length.
RegisterSession uses command 0x0065 with a 4-byte payload.
All status fields are zero.
All options fields are zero.
Length fields exactly match appended payload sizes.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: Stateful sequencing is limited to ordinary documented commands; no issue-derived behavior is claimed.

sequences.title: Connected explicit path with SendUnitData
sequences.purpose: Add coverage for the separate SendUnitData encapsulation command using the documented Connected Address Item plus Connected Data Item CPF combination and a small connected payload.
sequences.expected_behavior: The implementation should accept the SendUnitData header, parse the connected CPF item combination, and hand the small connected data item to subsequent handling.
constraints_preserved: Command 0x0070 is encoded little-endian as 7000.
Encapsulation length is 0x0018 and matches 24 bytes of command-specific data.
SendUnitData uses a 4-byte interface handle and 2-byte timeout before CPF.
CPF item_count is 2.
First CPF item is Connected Address Item 0x0100 with length 4 and a 4-byte address payload.
Second CPF item is Connected Data Item 0x00b1 with length 2 and a 2-byte data payload.
The documented common SendUnitData item combination is preserved.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: This is a conservative connected-path seed and avoids inventing larger connected transport structures.

sequences.title: Minimal valid SendRRData with full command-specific prefix
sequences.purpose: Repair earlier malformed SendRRData ideas by using the documented interface handle and timeout prefix followed by the common Null Address Item and a minimally non-empty Unconnected Data Item.
sequences.expected_behavior: The parser should accept a valid SendRRData command-specific structure, consume the CPF item count and the documented Null Address Item plus Unconnected Data Item combination, and forward the small unconnected payload.
constraints_preserved: Command 0x006f is encoded little-endian as 6f00.
Length field is 0x0012 and matches 18 command-specific bytes.
SendRRData prefix includes 4-byte interface handle and 2-byte timeout before CPF.
CPF item_count is 0x0002.
First item is Null Address Item 0x0000 with length 0.
Second item is Unconnected Data Item 0x00b2 with length 2.
All multibyte numeric fields are little-endian.
Command-specific data length is even.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: This replaces malformed prior transport shapes with a valid low-size structure and does not attempt any issue replay.

sequences.title: RegisterSession then UnregisterSession
sequences.purpose: Demonstrate a stateful session lifecycle by registering a session and then sending a syntactically valid UnregisterSession using a nonzero session handle.
sequences.expected_behavior: The parser should accept both messages as complete encapsulation commands and dispatch a session registration path followed by an unregister path.
constraints_preserved: RegisterSession uses command 0x0065 with length 4 and a 4-byte body.
UnregisterSession uses command 0x0066 with length 0.
Both messages preserve the 24-byte header layout.
Session handle in the unregister request is a 4-byte little-endian nonzero value.
Status and options are zero in both requests.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: This is a normal valid lifecycle sequence and does not assert semantic success of the chosen session handle beyond structural validity.

sequences.title: Message Router Get_Attributes_All over SendRRData
sequences.purpose: Provide a valid unconnected explicit message using SendRRData carrying a small Message Router request with service 0x01 and a class plus instance style path.
sequences.expected_behavior: The target should parse the outer SendRRData frame and CPF items, then attempt to dispatch a Get_Attributes_All Message Router request at CIP level.
constraints_preserved: Encapsulation length is 0x0018 and matches the 24-byte command-specific payload.
The SendRRData command-specific prefix contains interface handle 0 and timeout 0.
CPF uses the documented SendRRData item combination of Null Address Item and Unconnected Data Item.
Unconnected Data Item length is 8 and matches the embedded CIP request.
Service byte 0x01 is the documented Get_Attributes_All code.
Path-size byte is 0x02, matching two 16-bit words of path data.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: Depth comes from valid nested structure only; no malformed recursion or unsupported issue claim is included.

sequences.title: Unsupported CIP service in valid SendRRData envelope
sequences.purpose: Use a valid EtherNet/IP and CPF wrapper with an intentionally unsupported CIP service byte to reach ordinary CIP rejection logic associated with general status 0x08 Service Not Supported.
sequences.expected_behavior: The target should accept the EtherNet/IP and CPF framing and then reject the unsupported CIP service at the application layer rather than failing transport parsing.
constraints_preserved: Transport remains a valid SendRRData frame with a correct 24-byte header.
Length 0x0018 matches the command-specific bytes exactly.
The documented SendRRData CPF combination is preserved.
Unconnected Data Item length 8 matches the CIP request.
General status 0x08 Service Not Supported is cited as a possible CIP-layer outcome, not as a request operation.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: This is a safe negative-path structural seed using a valid envelope, with no malformed lengths and no issue enhancement.

sequences.title: Start service over valid SendRRData
sequences.purpose: Exercise CIP service code 0x06 within a correct SendRRData and CPF envelope to reach explicit-message service dispatch.
sequences.expected_behavior: The receiver should accept the encapsulation and CPF framing and then handle or reject the Start service request at CIP level rather than failing outer parsing.
constraints_preserved: SendRRData command is 0x006f.
Encapsulation length matches the 24 bytes after the header.
Interface handle and timeout are present before CPF.
CPF item_count is 2 with documented Null Address Item and Unconnected Data Item ordering.
Unconnected item length is 8 and matches the CIP bytes.
Service code 0x06 is the documented Start service.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: The seed stays within documented framing and uses a compact service request for safe initial coverage.

sequences.title: Stop service over valid SendRRData
sequences.purpose: Provide a structurally valid Stop service request carried by SendRRData to cover a neighboring CIP common service code with the same transport skeleton.
sequences.expected_behavior: The target should parse the valid SendRRData and CPF wrapper and then process or reject the Stop service request at the CIP layer.
constraints_preserved: Outer framing preserves the 24-byte encapsulation header.
Length is 0x0018, matching the 24-byte command-specific payload.
Command-specific data includes interface handle and timeout before CPF.
CPF order is item_count, Null Address Item, then Unconnected Data Item.
Service code 0x07 is the documented Stop service.
Path-size byte 0x02 matches the included path words.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: This is a valid service-bearing seed, not a malformed negative test.

sequences.title: Set_Attribute_Single with compact write data
sequences.purpose: Exercise a write-style CIP common service with class, instance, and attribute path segments plus a short service-data body.
sequences.expected_behavior: The receiver should parse the valid explicit-message transport and then process or reject the single-attribute write request at CIP level.
constraints_preserved: Encapsulation length is 0x001c and matches 28 command-specific bytes.
SendRRData uses interface handle and timeout before CPF.
CPF item_count is 2 with Null Address Item then Unconnected Data Item.
Unconnected item length is 12 and matches the CIP bytes.
Service code 0x10 is the documented Set_Attribute_Single service.
Path-size byte 0x03 matches the class-instance-attribute path.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: This seed is valid and compact, leaving payload growth to later mutations rather than forcing aggressive writes.

sequences.title: Get_Attribute_Single with attribute path
sequences.purpose: Cover a deeper Message Router path using class, instance, and attribute style addressing with a documented read-like CIP common service.
sequences.expected_behavior: The parser should accept the frame and CPF items and then reach CIP dispatch for a Get_Attribute_Single request with an attribute-bearing path.
constraints_preserved: Length field 0x001a matches the 26 bytes of command-specific data.
The command-specific prefix precedes CPF as required for SendRRData.
CPF item order and little-endian item headers are preserved.
Unconnected Data Item length 10 matches the embedded CIP request.
Service code 0x0e is the documented Get_Attribute_Single service.
Path-size byte 0x03 matches three 16-bit path words.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: This is a normal valid read-style request shape, not an error-oriented payload.

sequences.title: Set_Attributes_All with small service data
sequences.purpose: Exercise the interaction of a valid Message Router service code, a class-instance path, and a small service-data payload inside a correct SendRRData transport.
sequences.expected_behavior: The implementation should accept the valid encapsulation and CPF framing and then deliver a Set_Attributes_All request with two bytes of service data to higher-level handling.
constraints_preserved: Encapsulation length is 0x001a and matches 26 command-specific bytes.
SendRRData prefix includes interface handle and timeout.
CPF uses item_count 2, Null Address Item, and Unconnected Data Item.
Unconnected Data Item length is 10 and matches the CIP request size.
Service code 0x02 is the documented Set_Attributes_All service.
Path-size byte 0x02 matches the class-instance path.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: The small service-data block is mutation-friendly but remains structurally conservative.

global_feedback: The library has strong operation diversity and good intent to cover encapsulation, CPF, unconnected CIP, connected CPF, and simple stateful flows.
Several seeds are structurally useful, especially RegisterSession, discovery commands, UnregisterSession lifecycle, and the SendUnitData CPF shape.
A major recurring problem is inconsistency between stated length fields and the actual bytes present in multiple SendRRData seeds. This directly harms protocol validity and initial corpus quality.

Multiple CIP payloads appear to use noncanonical or insufficiently supported path segment encodings. The sources only document Message_Router fields generically, not specific path byte layouts used here.

Plans 007 and 014 are semantically awkward because they target response/status concepts rather than request operations; the unsupported-service negative path is acceptable structurally, but the plan mapping is weak.
For an initial seed corpus, fewer but more correct SendRRData examples would be preferable to many near-duplicates with questionable CIP internals.
Stateful coverage is present but could be improved by using a session-bearing SendRRData after RegisterSession rather than many standalone zero-session SendRRData requests.
To meet the desired selected seed count of 12, drop the weakest malformed or redundant SendRRData variants and keep the most defensible transport skeletons.

sequence_feedback.recommended_action: Keep as a canonical baseline RegisterSession seed.
Keep as a valid multi-message discovery plus registration sequence.

problems: The SendRRData wrapper is plausible, but the 2-byte unconnected data payload of 1400 is not a well-formed CIP Message Router request and may stop before deeper CIP parsing.
sequence_feedback.recommended_action: Keep only as a minimal CPF transport seed, or revise the unconnected data item to contain a valid minimal CIP request.

problems: The stated encapsulation length does not match the actual header field in the hex.
The embedded CIP path encoding is asserted as class/instance style, but the exact path bytes are not well supported by the provided sources.
sequence_feedback.recommended_action: Revise the outer length field to exactly match bytes after the 24-byte header and normalize the CIP request to a clearly valid Message Router encoding.

problems: The nonzero UnregisterSession handle is synthetic and not tied to a returned session handle from the prior RegisterSession response.
sequence_feedback.recommended_action: Keep for structural lifecycle coverage; optionally replace the hardcoded session handle with a captured valid one in a harness-aware corpus.

problems: The outer length/value commentary is inconsistent with the actual field value style seen elsewhere.
This is very close in structure to several other SendRRData CIP seeds, reducing marginal value.
The CIP path bytes are not strongly grounded by the sources.
sequence_feedback.recommended_action: Keep one of the simple Start or Stop variants, but revise lengths and CIP path encoding.

problems: Near-duplicate of the Start seed with only service code changed.
CIP path encoding is not clearly validated by the supplied evidence.
sequence_feedback.recommended_action: Keep only if retaining both neighboring service codes is important; otherwise prefer one of Start/Stop and drop the other.

problems: The encapsulation length statement conflicts with the actual hex field.
The embedded CIP payload length appears inconsistent with the stated Unconnected Data Item length.
Set_Attributes_All semantics typically require object-specific data; this compact form is unlikely to be broadly valid.
Plan/strategy metadata does not align cleanly with the supplied plan set.
sequence_feedback.recommended_action: Drop or fully rebuild with exact length accounting and a defensible CIP request body.

problems: The CIP body appears one byte short relative to the declared Unconnected Data Item length.
The path encoding for class/instance/attribute is not well substantiated from the sources.
sequence_feedback.recommended_action: Drop from the initial 12 unless corrected; if kept, fix the item length and CIP body size first.

problems: The write-style CIP payload is only weakly supported by the provided sources and may not be semantically acceptable to many targets.
Another close variant in a crowded SendRRData family.
sequence_feedback.recommended_action: Keep as one write-oriented CIP seed after verifying exact byte counts; otherwise replace with a simpler read-oriented valid request.

problems: The embedded CIP bytes do not clearly match the declared deeper four-word path and look undersized for the stated structure.
Length commentary and actual content are inconsistent.
Member-style path semantics are unsupported by the supplied evidence.
sequence_feedback.recommended_action: Drop from the selected set unless rebuilt from a documented valid Set_Member encoding.

problems: The declared Unconnected Data Item length does not appear to match the CIP bytes present.
Set_Attribute_List usually needs a more structured list body than provided here.
The seed is both structurally questionable and redundant with other write-style SendRRData seeds.
sequence_feedback.recommended_action: Drop from the initial corpus.

problems: This is intentionally negative at CIP service level, so it may not go as deep as valid service requests.
The plan target is a status outcome rather than a concrete request operation.
sequence_feedback.recommended_action: Keep as one structurally valid negative-path seed, but ensure it does not displace stronger valid requests.

problems: The connected address payload is synthetic and may not correspond to an established connection context.
sequence_feedback.recommended_action: Keep as the main SendUnitData/connected-CPF coverage seed.

coverage_gaps: A clearly valid session-bound SendRRData sequence after RegisterSession using a nonzero session handle is missing.
No high-confidence valid Unconnected_Send encoding from the Connection Manager service set is present despite plan coverage for it.
No Multiple_Service_Packet seed is included for deeper nested CIP parser coverage.
Discovery command coverage exists, but ListInterfaces, NOP, IndicateStatus, and Cancel are not represented as explicit individual seeds in the final selection guidance.
The corpus lacks a high-confidence valid Get_Attribute_List request, which would provide useful list parsing without the write-side semantic risk.
Several write-oriented CIP seeds should be replaced with fewer, better-validated Message Router requests whose path and payload sizes are unquestionably correct.

EtherNet/IP and CIP Function Code Reference
===========================================

Scope
-----
This file contains:

1. EtherNet/IP Encapsulation Commands
2. Common Packet Format Item Type IDs
3. CIP Common Service Codes
4. CIP Connection Manager Service Codes
5. CIP General Status Codes
6. Common CIP Object Class IDs
7. Response service-code rule

================================================================
1. ETHERNET/IP ENCAPSULATION COMMANDS
================================================================

0x0000 = NOP
0x0004 = ListServices
0x0063 = ListIdentity
0x0064 = ListInterfaces
0x0065 = RegisterSession
0x0066 = UnregisterSession
0x006F = SendRRData
0x0070 = SendUnitData
0x0072 = IndicateStatus
0x0073 = Cancel

Other values:
    Reserved or future encapsulation commands.

Command summary:

0x0000 NOP
    No-operation encapsulation command.

0x0004 ListServices
    Request supported encapsulation services.

0x0063 ListIdentity
    Discover EtherNet/IP device identity.

0x0064 ListInterfaces
    Request communication interfaces.

0x0065 RegisterSession
    Register an EtherNet/IP encapsulation session.

0x0066 UnregisterSession
    Unregister an active encapsulation session.

0x006F SendRRData
    Send unconnected request/response data.

0x0070 SendUnitData
    Send connected explicit or connected data.

0x0072 IndicateStatus
    Legacy encapsulation status indication.

0x0073 Cancel
    Cancel an outstanding request where supported.

================================================================
2. ENCAPSULATION HEADER FIELDS
================================================================

Command:
    2 bytes, little-endian

Length:
    2 bytes, little-endian

Session Handle:
    4 bytes, little-endian

Status:
    4 bytes, little-endian

24 bytes

0x00000002 = Insufficient memory resources
0x00000003 = Incorrect data in command

0x01 Get_Attributes_All
    Read all attributes supported by this service.

0x02 Set_Attributes_All
    Write all attributes supported by this service.

0x03 Get_Attribute_List
    Read selected attributes.

0x04 Set_Attribute_List

0x07 Stop

    Create an object instance.

0x09 Delete
    Delete an object instance.

global_feedback: The library has good breadth across encapsulation commands and SendRRData-based explicit messaging, but too many seeds have incorrect encapsulation length fields or malformed CPF ordering, which sharply reduces suitability as initial seeds.
RegisterSession baseline seed is the strongest item: complete 24-byte header, matching length, and conservative 4-byte body.
The stateful RegisterSession sequence is reasonable as a setup path, though the setup commands do not clearly deepen state for RegisterSession beyond basic sequential parsing.

Several SendRRData seeds omit the documented interface handle and timeout fields before CPF data, making their command-specific payloads questionable for protocol-valid SendRRData framing even when internal CPF pieces look consistent.
Multiple CIP-oriented seeds misorder CPF fields, use incorrect item lengths, or declare encapsulation lengths that do not match the actual bytes. These should not be kept unchanged.
Seeds targeting status values such as 'Success or no error in request' are weak coverage choices because they are not real request operations and add little beyond a generic NOP header parser path.
Issue enhancement is disabled, so neutral scoring is appropriate there; there is no copied crash payload concern visible, but protocol-framing errors are a larger practical problem.
Desired selected seed count is 12, but only a small subset is safe to keep as-is. Revision is required before a 12-seed final set is viable.

global_feedback: The library has strong operation diversity and good intent to cover encapsulation, CPF, unconnected CIP, connected CPF, and simple stateful flows.
Several seeds are structurally useful, especially RegisterSession, discovery commands, UnregisterSession lifecycle, and the SendUnitData CPF shape.
A major recurring problem is inconsistency between stated length fields and the actual bytes present in multiple SendRRData seeds. This directly harms protocol validity and initial corpus quality.

Multiple CIP payloads appear to use noncanonical or insufficiently supported path segment encodings. The sources only document Message_Router fields generically, not specific path byte layouts used here.

Plans 007 and 014 are semantically awkward because they target response/status concepts rather than request operations; the unsupported-service negative path is acceptable structurally, but the plan mapping is weak.
For an initial seed corpus, fewer but more correct SendRRData examples would be preferable to many near-duplicates with questionable CIP internals.
Stateful coverage is present but could be improved by using a session-bearing SendRRData after RegisterSession rather than many standalone zero-session SendRRData requests.
To meet the desired selected seed count of 12, drop the weakest malformed or redundant SendRRData variants and keep the most defensible transport skeletons.
